title: A Hubble gem: the Jewel Box
caption: The Jewel Box cluster NGC 4755, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4755 · constellation Crux · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA/ESA and Jesús Maíz Apellániz (Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía, Spain)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Several very bright, pale blue supergiant stars stand out in this close-up, along with a single ruby-red supergiant and a mix of other vividly coloured stars. Scattered among them are many much fainter stars, some with intriguing hues of their own. This is NGC 4755, better known as the Jewel Box cluster, seen by Hubble.

The Jewel Box is an open cluster, a group of stars that formed together and still travel as a family. Its members span a huge range of brightness because they span a wide range of mass. The brightest weigh in at 15 to 20 solar masses, whereas the faintest carry less than half the Sun's mass.

What makes this portrait special is its spread of light. It was the first image of an open galactic cluster to extend all the way from the far ultraviolet to the near-infrared, giving astronomers a view of these stars across a much wider range of wavelengths than the eye can see.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.51 x 1.24 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 4.7 × 2.3 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 observed the cluster through seven filters, from far-ultraviolet through visible to near-infrared. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are both invisible to the human eye, so much of the information in this picture lies outside what we could ever see directly.

explore: The cluster lies about 6500 light-years away. The image was made with Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 and is credited to NASA/ESA and Jesús Maíz Apellániz of the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía in Spain.
alt: A star cluster with several bright pale blue stars, one ruby-red star and many fainter, variously coloured stars.
